ANDROID · PRIVATE · INCREMENTAL

PersonalHub

A development blueprint for college, training, mood logging and Spotify listening history. Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, local storage, isolated feature modules, tested increments and explicit agent handoffs.

Planning baseline 1.1 · 12 November 2026 · No Android application has been built or device-tested in this package.

College

On-device VTOP connection, timetable, attendance, calendar, marks, grade history and transparent GPA scenarios.

Train

Exercise catalog, reusable routines, persistent set logging, rest timers, records and a muscle contribution map.

Focus

Usage and scrolling estimates, tested text/video classification, configured limits, daily tasks and private habits.

Proposed unified UI

These are original wireframes with synthetic data. Shared graphite surfaces, lime actions, bold headings, readable dense data and consistent navigation connect all sections. The body map is an illustrative region diagram.

New in version 1.1

Nine exact mood labels, unlimited timestamped entries, day/week/month graphs for moods, private manual counts, scrolling and workouts. Music is an independent final increment. Fully offline local data and charts; default daily JSON snapshots, seven-file retention, restore and scoped review exports.

Build → verify → add

StageResult
I00–I02Toolchain, installable shell and early VTOP/monitoring feasibility probes
I03Offline tasks, manual habits, Mood Log and early trend views
I04–I06Academic connection, attendance/calendar, marks/grades and scenarios
I07–I09Catalog/routines, live workouts/timers, history and muscle analytics
I10–I12Usage sessions, evaluated classifiers/scrolling, limits and derived habits
I13Regular local JSON backup/restore, offline/privacy/performance checks and core release candidate
I14 — finalSpotify/Music: local media capture, history/artwork, day/week/month stats; extend JSON and run final regressions

What needs proving

VTOP source inspection confirms the scraping approach, not live compatibility. Calendar availability and grade rules need validation. Text/video detection is source/version dependent. Blocking redirects away from a target; it does not promise Android process termination. Exercise animation rights must be cleared individually. Spotify capture and images depend on exposed/obtainable metadata and need device validation; unsupported history or artwork is never invented.
